papers.title: Accelerating ligand screening for tuberculosis: predicting binding energies with a 3D deep neural network.
papers.abstract: The computational burden of molecular docking becomes prohibitive when receptor flexibility is explicitly considered, despite the accuracy gained in virtual screening workflows. To mitigate this limitation, we introduce a three-dimensional deep neural network designed to estimate binding energies before exhaustive docking across the complete fully flexible receptor ensemble. We target the InhA enzyme, a validated target of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, through the use of a fully flexible receptor model (with 20,000 poses) generated by computational simulation. The model leverages volumetric repr
papers.summary: This paper presents a 3D deep neural network that predicts ligand binding energies for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis InhA enzyme, aiming to bypass the computational cost of exhaustive docking against a fully flexible receptor ensemble. Using a receptor model with 20,000 poses, the approach screens ligands more efficiently while retaining flexibility-aware accuracy. It offers a practical speedup for virtual screening in tuberculosis drug discovery.

papers.title: Site-Specific Features Guiding Effective Reversible Photocontrol of Tryptophan Synthase With the Unnatural Amino Acid AzoF.
papers.abstract: This study delivers initial guidelines for the selection of effective incorporation positions for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF to facilitate the successful engineering of light-sensitive enzymes, dubbed photoxenases. Although photoxenases gain interest for the photocontrol of enzymatic activity across various fields their design has so far remained challenging. To ease particularly the selection of AzoF incorporation sites, we have systematically evaluated a total of 85 positions that differ in their biochemical and biophysical features in the bi-enzyme model system tryptopha
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates 85 different incorporation sites for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF in tryptophan synthase to identify features that enable effective reversible photocontrol of enzyme activity. The authors provide initial guidelines for selecting positions that yield light-sensitive 'photoxenases,' addressing a key bottleneck in engineering photoswitchable enzymes.

papers.title: Computational and Data-Driven Strategies for Lignocellulosic Biomass Valorization: From Multiscale Modeling to Digitalized Biorefinery Design.
papers.abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is a major renewable carbon resource for sustainable production of fuels, chemicals, and functional materials. Yet its valorization remains constrained by structural recalcitrance, feedstock heterogeneity, and the coupling of molecular and process phenomena. This review critically examines computational and data-driven strategies for predictive biorefinery development, with emphasis on how experimentally anchored information can be transferred across scales. Structural determinants of deconstructability, including cellulose organization, lignin chemistry, lignin-carbohy
papers.summary: This review surveys computational and data-driven approaches for converting lignocellulosic biomass into fuels, chemicals, and materials, focusing on how experimental data can be transferred across molecular, material, and process scales. It highlights structural factors like cellulose organization and lignin chemistry that govern biomass recalcitrance, and discusses pathways toward digitalized, predictive biorefinery design.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors developed MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat measurements, and demonstrated that the model can guide rational enzyme evolution.

papers.title: Microbial production of eumelanin from a desert-derived Aspergillus terreus: statistical optimization, comprehensive characterization, and in silico insights into breast cancer-associated targets.
papers.abstract: Naturally derived microbial products are increasingly explored as sustainable sources of bioactive compounds for targeted cancer applications. Among these, eumelanin is a nitrogen-containing polymeric pigment produced by various microorganisms, including fungi, and is distinguished by its unique physicochemical properties, biocompatibility, and free radical scavenging capacity. Nevertheless, eumelanin-producing fungi from extreme desert habitats remain poorly explored, particularly those isolated from the Wadi Allaqi Biosphere Reserve, and comprehensive studies integrating production optimizat
papers.summary: This study isolated a eumelanin-producing Aspergillus terreus strain from the Wadi Allaqi desert biosphere reserve and optimized its production using statistical methods, followed by comprehensive physicochemical characterization. The authors also performed in silico docking analyses suggesting the eumelanin may interact with breast cancer-associated molecular targets, hinting at potential anticancer applications.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that the classical view of GPCRs as isolated monomers is outdated, as converging structural, biophysical, and pharmacological evidence shows these receptors act as dynamic homo- and heteromeric complexes in brain regions relevant to neuropsychiatric disease. The authors suggest that targeting GPCR heteromers could improve efficacy and reduce side effects for patients who respond poorly to current monomer-directed drugs.

papers.title: Design and computational investigation of a polyaniline-pyrrole copolymer and its antimicrobial and cytotoxic properties.
papers.abstract: The present study focused on the single-pot synthesis of polyaniline (PANI) and polyaniline-pyrrole (PANI-Py) copolymer via the chemical oxidative polymerization method (COPM). The structural features of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py were characterised using UV-visible and FTIR spectroscopy. The thermal stability of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py copolymer was examined by TGA and DSC over the temperature range of 33-1000 °C. BET and viscosity measurements analysed surface area and molecular weight. Conductivity of PANI and PANI-Py was measured by a two-probe method. DFT calculations confirmed the
papers.summary: This study synthesizes a polyaniline-pyrrole copolymer via chemical oxidative polymerization and characterizes its structural, thermal, and conductive properties using spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and DFT calculations. The authors also evaluate its antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity, suggesting potential biomedical applications for the conducting copolymer.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening guided by specific criteria to identify HDAC3 inhibitors that use alternative zinc-binding groups instead of the typical hydroxamate. The goal is to find more selective inhibitors with better pharmacokinetic profiles, since hydroxamate-based inhibitors are potent but non-selective. The approach prioritizes HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate zinc coordination.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: This paper introduces a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. The approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods (like CLEAN and ProteInter) and global structural alignment tools, which either miss fine-grained distinctions or produce high false positive rates for globally similar proteins.

papers.title: [Rational design for improving the thermostability of β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans].
papers.abstract: The β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans (Bgl52) has been identified as a thermophilic and acidophilic β-glucosidase, which constitutes the most critical component in the cellulolytic enzyme system for cellulose hydrolysis. Although Bgl52 is a thermophilic enzyme, its poor thermal stability at high temperatures restricts its long-term industrial application under elevated-temperature conditions. In this study, rational design strategies, including two free energy calculation programs (Fireprot and FoldX) and homologous sequence alignment, were integrated to perform single-point and mu
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used rational design strategies—including the free energy calculation tools Fireprot and FoldX, plus homologous sequence alignment—to engineer the thermophilic β-glucosidase Bgl52 from Bacillus thermoamylovorans for improved thermal stability. The goal was to overcome the enzyme's poor stability at high temperatures, which limits its long-term industrial use in cellulose hydrolysis.

papers.title: [Rational design and molecular engineering of a chitosanase for preparing specific chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization≥5].
papers.abstract: To achieve efficient enzymatic preparation of specific high-degree-of-polymerization chito-oligosaccharides (degree of polymerization≥5, DP≥5), rational molecular engineering of chitosanase Csn46-Mut4 was performed in this study. Through site-directed mutagenesis coupled with DNS enzyme activity-HPLC product distribution screening, a superior mutant, C41A/T47A/V144A, was obtained. Under conditions of 55℃ and pH 5.5, the catalytic efficiency and thermostability of this enzyme were remarkably enhanced, reaching 2.56-fold and 1.67-fold those of Csn46-Mut4, respectively. Peak area normalization an
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study used rational design and site-directed mutagenesis to engineer a chitosanase variant (C41A/T47A/V144A) with improved catalytic efficiency and thermostability for producing chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization ≥5. The engineered enzyme showed 2.56-fold higher catalytic efficiency and 1.67-fold better thermostability than the parent enzyme, enabling more efficient preparation of these specific oligosaccharides.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTACs, molecules that degrade target proteins by recruiting E3 ubiquitin ligases. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing a key gap in computational PROTAC design.

papers.title: Spontaneous Phase Separation in Polymer Solution by Janus Nanoparticle Compatibilizers: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We perform atomistic molecular dynamics simulations in order to investigate the structural and dynamic properties of Janus gold nanoparticles within diverse solvent environments, specifically pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water matrices. The nanoparticles, approximately 7 nm in diameter and almost totally surrounded by (211) surfaces at the thermodynamic limit, are functionalized with hydrophobic polyethylene chains on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly-(ethylene oxide) chains on the other. In mixed systems, the Janus nanoparticle acts as an effective stabilizer, direc
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to examine how Janus gold nanoparticles (with hydrophobic polyethylene on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly(ethylene oxide) on the other) behave in pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water environments. The authors find that in mixed systems, the Janus nanoparticles act as effective compatibilizers, directing the spontaneous phase separation of the polymer solution by stabilizing the interface between the immiscible phases.

papers.title: Unraveling the Complex Hydrogen-Bonding and Solvation Patterns of Fructose Tautomers via Complementary AIMD and Classical MD Simulations.
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular-level hydration of fructose tautomers remains a challenge due to their rapid interconversion and structural complexity. A dual-scale approach was employed, combining long-time classical molecular dynamics (MD) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to elucidate differences in the hydrogen-bonding networks of both pyranose and furanose tautomers with statistical and electronic accuracy. Our simulations highlight the inherent competition between intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonds, driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites. Crucially, the
papers.summary: This study uses a dual-scale simulation approach, combining classical molecular dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics, to investigate how fructose tautomers (pyranose and furanose forms) interact with water through hydrogen bonding. The simulations reveal a competition between intramolecular and intermolecular hydrogen bonds, driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites on each tautomer. The work provides molecular-level insight into fructose hydration patterns that could inform understanding of sugar behavior in biological and chemical systems.

papers.title: Targeting DYRK1A with rationally designed pyrazine-guanidine hybrids for Alzheimer's disease: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) has been implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by regulating tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammatory pathways, suggesting DYRK1A as an important therapeutic target. Herein, we report the rational design, synthesis and evaluation of a new class of low-molecular-weight pyrazine-guanidine molecular hybrids as potential DYRK1A inhibitors via an integrated computational and experimental approach. Molecular docking studies predicted good protein-ligand interactions, with compounds F1, F5, and F7 exhibi
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazine-guanidine hybrid molecules intended to inhibit DYRK1A, a kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease through tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammation. Using molecular docking followed by experimental evaluation, compounds F1, F5, and F7 showed promising protein-ligand interactions, suggesting these hybrids could serve as leads for DYRK1A-targeted AD therapeutics.

papers.title: Solvent Extraction for Heavy Oil from Carbonate AsphaltsExperiment and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We have systematically studied the effects of solvents such as benzene, toluene, isooctane, and cyclooctane on the selective separation of four heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes), aiming to clarify the molecular mechanism of solvent extraction as an oil-solid separation method in heavy oil extraction. However, the time-dependent extraction kinetics and the detachment behavior of different saturates, aromatics, resins, and asphaltenes (SARA) fractions from mineral surfaces under solvent action remain insufficiently understood. In this work, solvent extraction exper
papers.summary: This study combines solvent extraction experiments with molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how solvents like benzene, toluene, isooctane, and cyclooctane selectively separate heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes) from carbonate asphalt surfaces. The work aims to clarify the molecular mechanisms and kinetics of oil-solid separation, particularly how different SARA fractions detach from mineral surfaces under solvent action.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify variants of uncertain significance, which could guide treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer. It offers a computational framework for prioritizing mutations for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Monoterpene Phenol Dimers from Satureja bachtiarica.
papers.abstract: Satureja bachtiarica (Bakhtiari savory) is an aromatic herb cultivated both as a culinary spice and for its medicinal uses. Species of Satureja are known to exhibit anti-inflammatory properties. Monoterpene phenol dimers with biphenyl skeletons have been identified in these plants and structural investigations revealed the key role of the biphenyl scaffold in interacting with MAPEG family proteins. Thus, in the present contribution, we investigated by biochemical and cell-based assays, together with molecular docking and molecular dynamics investigations, the modulation of inflammatory mediato
papers.summary: This study investigates monoterpene phenol dimers from the herb Satureja bachtiarica, focusing on their anti-inflammatory properties. Using biochemical and cell-based assays alongside molecular docking and dynamics simulations, the authors show that the biphenyl scaffold of these compounds interacts with MAPEG family proteins to modulate inflammatory mediators. The findings highlight the potential of these plant-derived dimers as leads for anti-inflammatory drug development.

papers.title: Insights into the Solution Structure and Oligomeric State of Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate Aldolase and Pyruvate Kinase from Nakaseomyces glabratus by Small-Angle X‑ray Scattering (SAXS) and AlphaFold Prediction.
papers.abstract: Nakaseomyces glabratus is an opportunistic pathogen of humans, causing invasive candidiasis (IC). Among the risk factors that favor IC are various host-specific factors. Although drugs are available to treat candidiasis, their clinical application remains limited. Therefore, it is necessary to identify therapeutic targets that will enable the development of new antifungals. In this regard, our research group has identified enzymes as potential therapeutic targets in N. glabratus, including fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk). Enzyme activity studies on these two
papers.summary: This study uses small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) combined with AlphaFold structure prediction to characterize the solution structure and oligomeric state of two potential antifungal drug targets—fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk)—from the human fungal pathogen Nakaseomyces glabratus. The work provides structural insights that could support the development of new therapeutics against invasive candidiasis.

papers.title: Alchemical Free Energy Perturbation Predicts Relative Binding Affinities of Propofol Analogs and Etomidate Stereoisomers at the GABAAR.
papers.abstract: General anesthetics such as propofol and etomidate exert their clinical effects primarily through positive allosteric modulation of γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors (GABAAR). Despite decades of research, the quantitative structure-activity relationships governing anesthetic binding remain incompletely characterized at the atomic level. Here, we employ rigorous alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations using a CHARMm GPU-accelerated protocol to compute relative binding free energies for a series of 13 propofol analogs at the wild-type GABAAR, as well as for the stereoisomeric p
papers.summary: This study applies alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations to predict relative binding affinities of propofol analogs and etomidate stereoisomers at the GABA-A receptor. The work demonstrates that rigorous FEP can quantitatively capture structure-activity relationships for general anesthetics at this important drug target. The findings support the use of FEP as a tool for understanding and potentially designing anesthetic compounds.

papers.title: Multiscale Investigation of Triboelectric Nanogenerator: An Expanded DFT Calculation Based on Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Various types of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have been proposed, which rely on the details of electron transfer, ion migration, and mechanochemistry, but their largely different scales complicate the quantitative analysis of their contributions. In this study, we first investigate the electron transfer behavior at the nanoscale using density functional theory (DFT) calculations for the contact of two typical insulating materials, poly-(vinyl chloride) (PVC) and poly-(vinyl alcohol) (PVA), with an adsorbed water layer in between. The DFT results are then used to construct machine learn
papers.summary: This study combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations with machine learning to model electron transfer in triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), focusing on the contact between PVC and PVA with an adsorbed water layer. The DFT results are used to train machine learning models that extend the analysis across multiple scales, addressing the challenge of bridging nanoscale electron transfer with larger-scale device behavior.

papers.title: Exploring the Inhibitory Effects of Some Detergents on Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis with Specific Focus on Zwitterionic Sulfobetaines.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP) infects ruminants with Johne's disease and is also involved in human inflammatory bowel syndrome, such as Crohn's disease. With increasing drug resistance and zoonosis, there is a critical need for novel antimicrobial compounds having the potential to inhibit disease-causing bacteria. The present work examines the antimycobacterial activity of six detergent-like compounds, among which four are sulfobetaine-based zwitterionic detergents: amidosulfobetaine-14 (ASB-14), lauryl sulfobetaine (DDAPS), caprylyl sulfobetaine (D4266), and sulfobetai
papers.summary: This study tested six detergent-like compounds, including four zwitterionic sulfobetaines, for their ability to inhibit Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP), a bacterium causing Johne's disease in ruminants and linked to Crohn's disease in humans. The sulfobetaine detergents showed antimycobacterial activity, suggesting these compounds could serve as leads for novel antimicrobials against drug-resistant MAP.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a de novo protein design framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to engineer a thermostable diagnostic antigen derived from the yellow fever virus NS1 protein. By mapping the evolutionary dynamics of the YFV polyprotein, they identified conserved but discriminating regions to reduce cross-reactivity with related arboviruses, aiming to improve serological assay specificity and cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: S100A8/A9-TMEM24 axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy: A novel theranostic target for early diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: To establish a comprehensive theranostic framework for early-stage diabetic kidney disease (DKD) by validating serum S100A8/A9 as a highly sensitive diagnostic biomarker and exploring therapeutic strategies targeting the S100A9/transmembrane protein 24 (TMEM24) signaling axis to restore podocyte autophagy.
papers.summary: This study identifies serum S100A8/A9 as a sensitive biomarker for early diabetic kidney disease and shows that the S100A9-TMEM24 signaling axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy. Targeting this axis may offer a new therapeutic strategy to restore podocyte function in early diabetic nephropathy.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review discusses metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy to overcome the blood-brain barrier and treat brain disorders like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, highlighting their potential for improved brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Molecular glues: Recent advances in cereblon substrate identification and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: This highlight summarizes the recent advances in cereblon (CRBN) substrate discovery and mechanisms of action within the field of molecular glues. It emphasizes that molecular glue technology has transitioned from the stage of monofunctional targeted protein degradation to that of rational design and multidimensional regulation. Key recent breakthroughs include: (1) overcoming the limitations of canonical CRBN recognition motifs, identifying extensive novel substrates and unconventional recognition modes independent of fixed specific secondary structures; (2) reconceptualizing G protein-couple
papers.summary: This highlight reviews recent progress in understanding how molecular glues recruit the E3 ligase cereblon (CRBN) to degrade target proteins. It emphasizes a shift from serendipitous monofunctional degradation toward rational design, including the discovery of novel CRBN substrates and unconventional recognition modes that do not rely on canonical structural motifs.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis and Antihyperglycemic/Antilipidemic Activities of Quinoline-thiazolidine-2,4-dione Hybrid.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and hyperlipidemia are interrelated metabolic disorders that significantly increase cardiovascular risk. Thiazolidinediones are known insulin sensitizers, whereas quinoline derivatives possess diverse pharmacological activities. To explore their complementary activity, we designed a novel hybrid compound integrating a thiazolidinedione core with a quinoline moiety via a carbon spacer. Materials and Methods: The hybrid molecule was synthesized through a straightforward route and structurally confirmed by spectroscopic analyses. Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
papers.summary: This paper reports the design and synthesis of a new hybrid molecule combining a quinoline moiety with a thiazolidine-2,4-dione core, aiming to treat both type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia. The compound was structurally confirmed by spectroscopy and evaluated for antihyperglycemic and antilipidemic activity using a zebrafish model. The hybrid approach seeks to leverage the complementary pharmacological properties of both scaffolds in a single agent.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) based on active site properties rather than sequence alone. By using structural features of the enzyme active site as ML inputs, the approach captures sequence-function relationships that are difficult to infer from sequence data. This offers a data-driven route to classifying and potentially engineering these industrially relevant enzymes.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer potential. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro for antibacterial activity, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. The work identifies these scaffolds as promising starting points for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, causing a shift from large micelles to smaller, dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest these enzyme-biosurfactant composites could improve interfacial activity for petroleum engineering applications.

papers.title: High-throughput physics-based enzyme engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering aims to tailor natural enzymes for industrial and therapeutic applications, yet physically grounded rational design has been limited by a trade-off between accuracy and cost, leaving the field heavily dependent on expert intuition. Here we present a scalable physics-based framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to capture enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while enabling efficient, atomistic exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes. Coupled with microkinetic modelling, the framework translates molecular free-energ
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a scalable physics-based enzyme engineering framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to model enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. By coupling this with microkinetic modeling, the approach enables high-throughput exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes and rational enzyme design without relying on expert intuition.

papers.title: Engineered mRNA nanostructures expand the design space of mRNA therapeutics through programmable protein expression and immune stimulation.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have transformed vaccination and protein replacement strategies, yet efforts to improve their performance have focused largely on sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, and delivery vehicles. Here we show that mRNA function can be controlled by rational design of higher-order RNA architectures. We develop self-assembling mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of unimolecular RNA nanostructures that encode protein-coding sequences within higher-order, programmable, and compact nucleic acid architectures. Using computational design and experimental validation,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of self-assembling, unimolecular RNA nanostructures that embed protein-coding sequences within programmable higher-order architectures. By rationally designing these structures, the authors show that mRNA function—including protein expression levels and immune stimulation—can be tuned independently of sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, or delivery vehicles. This expands the design space for mRNA therapeutics beyond conventional sequence-level optimization.

papers.title: Cracking ERα Y537S Resistance: Explainable Machine Learning-Guided Discovery and Molecular Dynamics Validation of Stable Candidate Ligands.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Endocrine resistance due to activating mutations in the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα), especially Y537S, is still a big challenge in the treatment of hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and there is a need to develop new small-molecule inhibitors that can overcome ligand-independent receptor activation. We used an integrated machine learning and molecular dynamics (MD)-based virtual screening (VS) approach to identify potential computationally prioritized hits of ERα Y537S in this study. Methods: The dataset (~3353 compounds) was characterized using molecular finger
papers.summary: This study combines explainable machine learning with molecular dynamics simulations to discover small-molecule ligands that can overcome the Y537S mutation in estrogen receptor alpha, a key driver of endocrine resistance in breast cancer. The authors screened ~3,353 compounds and prioritized candidate hits, then validated their stability through MD simulations. The work offers a computational pipeline for identifying inhibitors that target mutant ERα rather than relying on traditional ligand-binding strategies.

papers.title: Identification of Small-Molecule Inhibitors of Babesia bovis by High-Throughput SYBR Green I Screening.
papers.abstract: Background: Bovine babesiosis, caused by Babesia bovis, remains a major constraint to cattle production in endemic regions, while the current control relies on only a few drugs with concerns over resistance and residues. Methods: This study screened 9600 chemically diverse compounds from the Drug Discovery Initiative, University of Tokyo, against B. bovis using a 96-well SYBR Green I high-throughput assay at 1 µM. Primary hits were subjected to dose-response testing to determine IC50 values, followed by Madin-Darby bovine kidney cell cytotoxicity assays for selectivity index calculation. Combi
papers.summary: This study screened 9,600 chemically diverse compounds against the cattle parasite Babesia bovis using a high-throughput SYBR Green I assay, identifying primary hits that were then validated with dose-response and cytotoxicity testing to determine IC50 values and selectivity indices. The work provides new candidate small-molecule inhibitors to address drug resistance and residue concerns in bovine babesiosis control.

papers.title: TRPM8 virtual screening: the essential role of target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions.
papers.abstract: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein confo
papers.summary: This paper establishes the first comprehensive structure-based virtual screening benchmark for the TRPM8 ion channel, a therapeutic target for pain and inflammation. It compares classical docking scoring functions, generic machine-learning scoring functions, and target-specific ML models across multiple TRPM8 protein conformations. The key finding is that target-specific, inactive-enriched ML scoring functions substantially improve virtual screening performance for this challenging ion channel target.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This study introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that replaces the standard multilayer perceptron in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation. The model combines molecular graph representations with a convolutional protein sequence encoder and was benchmarked on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ against a matched GIN baseline. The work tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves affinity prediction over conventional architectures.

papers.title: Anti-HIV Potential of Origanum vulgare Compounds Targeting Viral Reverse Transcriptase with High Binding and Stability Validated by Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is one of the viruses that has co-evolved within human populations for a considerable time. With the evolution of new drug-resistant HIV strains, the necessity to discover novel drugs has become an issue of great concern, especially those that have increased binding affinities and inhibitory activity towards RT enzymes. This study used an in silico approach to identify potential HIV-RT inhibitory candidates from Origanum vulgare (oregano). An initial in silico screening of approximately 820 compounds was conducted, and based on molecular docking-derived bindi
papers.summary: This study used computational docking and machine learning to screen ~820 compounds from oregano (Origanum vulgare) for their ability to bind and inhibit HIV reverse transcriptase. Several candidates showed high binding affinity and stability, suggesting oregano-derived compounds could be starting points for anti-HIV drug development. The findings are entirely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Pangenome-Guided In Silico Design and Structural Evaluation of a Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Streptococcus suis.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives:Streptococcus suis is an important zoonotic pathogen responsible for severe infections in animals and humans, and the emergence of diverse strains has reduced the effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial therapies. Since there is no broadly protective vaccine, there is a need for new vaccination strategies that focus on conserved antigens from a variety of strains. This study aimed to design and evaluate a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against diverse S. suis strains using an integrated pangenome-guided reverse vaccinology approach. Methods: To design a multi-epitope
papers.summary: This study used a pangenome-guided reverse vaccinology approach to design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against diverse strains of Streptococcus suis, a zoonotic pathogen lacking a broadly protective vaccine. The authors identified conserved antigens across strains and structurally evaluated the resulting multi-epitope construct in silico.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates current practices in molecular docking of natural products, highlighting that methodological quality remains highly variable despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines how different natural-product classes and protein targets require tailored docking approaches and calls for standardized guidelines. The paper provides practical recommendations to improve rigor and reproducibility in natural-product docking studies.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The approach leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose approved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: Dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-ones and Benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-ones: Useful Scaffolds for Development of Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitors †.
papers.abstract: Modulation of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) by small molecules is a vital strategy in drug discovery. Nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of PPI interfaces, practical implementation of this approach remains a high-hanging fruit in medicinal chemistry. In this report, we develop a new line of PEX14-PEX5 PPI inhibitors by homologation of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold. The challenging chemistry of 8-membered ring formation led to the development of novel PEX14 inhibitors featuring a 6+8+6 tricyclic system. The obtained analogs were tested for their capabi
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of novel dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-one and benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-one scaffolds, which are 8-membered ring homologs of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold, for use as protein-protein interaction (PPI) inhibitors. The authors used these scaffolds to develop new inhibitors of the PEX14-PEX5 interaction, demonstrating the potential of these tricyclic systems in medicinal chemistry.

papers.title: Optimization of dsRNA Length and Target Position for Enhanced RNA Interference Efficiency Targeting the Chitinase Gene MsChi2 in Mythimna separata.
papers.abstract: Chitinase is a key enzyme involved in insect chitin metabolism, and RNA interference (RNAi) targeting the corresponding gene represents a promising strategy for eco-friendly pest management. However, the design parameters of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), particularly fragment length and target position, remain insufficiently optimized. To investigate the effects of these parameters on the RNAi efficiency against the MsChi2 gene in Mythimna separata, we synthesized four dsRNAs of 60, 200, 500, and 1000 bp and administered them to larvae. The results indicated that 200 and 500 bp dsRNAs significa
papers.summary: This study tested how the length and target position of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) affect RNA interference efficiency against the chitinase gene MsChi2 in the armyworm Mythimna separata. They found that 200 and 500 bp dsRNA fragments produced significantly better gene silencing than 60 or 1000 bp fragments, suggesting an optimal intermediate length for pest control applications.

papers.title: Comprehensive Characterization of Cytochrome P450s Reveals Candidate Enzymes Involved in the Metabolic Fate of Absorbed Volatile Organic Compounds in Potato.
papers.abstract: Plants are continuously exposed to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by neighbors. Although the mechanisms governing VOC uptake and metabolism remain unclear, cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYP450s) are thought to participate in the detoxification and metabolic conversion of absorbed VOCs. Data from previously conducted cDNA microarray transcriptomic profiling in potato exposed to French marigold essential oil (FM-EO) was here used to filter differentially expressed sequences, and identified 54 unique CYP450 transcripts. Among the 10 most highly expressed sequences, two CYP81D1-like (
papers.summary: The study identifies 54 cytochrome P450 transcripts in potato that respond to absorbed volatile organic compounds from French marigold essential oil, with two CYP81D1-like enzymes emerging as top candidates for VOC detoxification and metabolism. This provides a foundation for understanding how plants process airborne chemicals from neighboring plants.

papers.title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Antibody Design: From Structure-Based Engineering to Generative Models.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed computational antibody engineering by enabling accurate prediction of antibody structures, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design. Recent advances in deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI have fundamentally changed the way antibodies are discovered and engineered. This review aims to present the historical evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design strategies to modern AI-driven approaches, while highlighting the major computation
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design to modern AI-driven methods like deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI. It highlights how these advances enable accurate antibody structure prediction, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design.

papers.title: Rational Design of Aspergillus awamori Glucoamylase for Activity Improvement.
papers.abstract: Glucoamylases are highly demanded by the industry for starch saccharification, which necessitates an increase in enzyme activity. To improve the activity of Aspergillus awamori VKPM F-1262 glucoamylase N181Q (AGAM), amino acid substitutions were made in the region of substrate binding. In the case of the variant D237G, there was a 1.3-1.4-fold increase in activity towards soluble starch for the individual enzyme and crude enzyme solution after cultivation in flasks. For the variants G57A and C319T, there was also a 1.1-1.4-fold increase in enzyme activity for the crude flask solution, while th
papers.summary: This study rationally engineered Aspergillus awamori glucoamylase by introducing amino acid substitutions in the substrate-binding region to improve starch saccharification activity. Variants D237G, G57A, and C319T showed modest increases (1.1–1.4-fold) in activity toward soluble starch, with D237G performing best in both purified and crude enzyme preparations.

papers.title: Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship Approaches for Exploring the Anticancer Potential of Flavonoids.
papers.abstract: Flavonoids are structurally diverse polyphenolic compounds widely distributed in fruits, vegetables, grains, and beverages, with considerable potential as anticancer agents. Their pleiotropic activities involve modulation of key cancer hallmarks, including oxidative stress, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, autophagy, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastasis. These effects are mediated through multiple signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT3. Understanding the relationship between flavonoid structure and biological activity is therefore essential for rational optimization
papers.summary: This review examines how quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) approaches can be used to understand and optimize the anticancer properties of flavonoids. It highlights how flavonoid structural features influence their modulation of cancer hallmarks such as oxidative stress, apoptosis, and metastasis through pathways like PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT3. The work aims to guide rational design of flavonoid-based anticancer agents.

papers.title: Antifungal Activity of Hedychium spicatum Essential Oil Against Candidemia-Causing Candida tropicalis and Candida parapsilosis: In Vitro Evaluation and Computational Identification of Cis-γ-Bisabolene as a Putative CYP51-Binding Constituent.
papers.abstract: Candidiasis is caused by Candida parapsilosis and Candida tropicalis emerges due to antifungal resistance and limited therapies. We aim to assess the antifungal activity of Hedychium spicatum essential oil (HSEO), followed by computational analyses to identify potential lead phytochemicals, targeting lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51), a key enzyme in ergosterol biosynthesis. GC-MS identified 29 phytoconstituents, with τ-cadinol (17.94%) as the major component. Disc diffusion demonstrated concentration-dependent antifungal activity against C. parapsilosis and C. tropicalis, with inhibition zon
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antifungal activity of Hedychium spicatum essential oil against two candidemia-causing Candida species, showing concentration-dependent inhibition. GC-MS identified 29 constituents, and computational docking pinpointed cis-γ-bisabolene as a putative binder of the fungal target CYP51, suggesting a possible mechanism for the oil's activity.

papers.title: State-dependent inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels by DCPIB.
papers.abstract: DCPIB is the prototypical inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat containing protein 8 volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), yet the structural basis and state dependence of inhibition remain unclear. Here, we used chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to define the determinants of DCPIB inhibition and elucidate how drug binding is coupled to channel gating. Effective inhibition required coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 (EL1) and transmembrane domain 2 (TM2), which together form a functional module governing access to and stabilization of DCPIB-bound sta
papers.summary: This study identifies the structural determinants of DCPIB inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels, showing that extracellular loop 1 and transmembrane domain 2 work together to control drug access and binding. The findings reveal that DCPIB inhibition is state-dependent, coupling drug binding to channel gating.

papers.title: Integrated computational and experimental identification of a novel ML-IAP-targeting peptide with antiproliferative activity in leukaemia cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma inhibitor of apoptosis protein (ML-IAP) is an IAP family member involved in tumour cell survival and a potential target in ML-IAP-expressing leukaemia. Here, 59 319 tetrapeptides were screened against ML-IAP by molecular docking, and four top-ranked peptides were selected. Microscale thermophoresis confirmed binding of peptides 1-4 to ML-IAP, with peptide-1 showing the lowest Kd value and a lower Kd value than the Smac peptide. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that peptide-1 had more favourable ML-IAP recognition features. A molecular dynamics simulation, molec
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study screened 59,319 tetrapeptides against the anti-apoptotic protein ML-IAP using molecular docking, then experimentally validated four top candidates with microscale thermophoresis. Peptide-1 bound ML-IAP most tightly (better than the natural Smac peptide) and showed antiproliferative activity in leukaemia cells, suggesting a promising starting point for developing ML-IAP-targeting therapeutics.

papers.title: Molecular insights into triazole-based compounds for triple-negative breast cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive breast cancer subtype lacking oestrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors, thus limiting the effectiveness of targeted therapies. Triazole compounds have emerged as promising anticancer agents because of their structural versatility, chemical stability, and ability to interact with multiple biological targets. This review summarises the chemistry, biological significance, and therapeutic potential of triazole derivatives against TNBC. It highlights key anticancer mechanisms, including apoptosis induction, cell cycle arrest, inhibition of an
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This review summarizes the chemistry and therapeutic potential of triazole-based compounds against triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), an aggressive subtype lacking targeted receptor therapies. It highlights anticancer mechanisms such as apoptosis induction, cell cycle arrest, and inhibition of key molecular targets, positioning triazoles as versatile scaffolds for TNBC drug development.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that enhances the catalytic activity of GSTP1, an enzyme often silenced in prostate cancer. Using structure-based screening and biochemical assays, the authors show Crocin I binds GSTP1 and increases its enzymatic Vmax without significantly affecting substrate affinity. This suggests a potential strategy to boost residual GSTP1 activity in prostate adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Simulation Reveal Potential Targets and Pathways of Vine Tea in Feline Intestinal Inflammation.
papers.abstract: Feline intestinal inflammation is a common gastrointestinal disorder in cats and is associated with immune dysregulation, epithelial barrier injury, microbial imbalance, and persistent inflammatory signaling. This entirely in silico study investigated predicted molecular associations between vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) constituents and feline intestinal inflammation using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. No feline cells, tissues, animals, or clinical samples were used. Candidate compounds were screened and evaluated with SwissADME as a computa
papers.summary: This entirely in silico study used network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation to predict molecular targets and pathways through which vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata) constituents might act against feline intestinal inflammation. No feline cells, tissues, animals, or clinical samples were used, so all findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Accelerating Cosmetic Innovation Through Next-Generation Computational Toxicology: From Structural Alerts to Molecular Dynamics and Artificial Intelligence for Skin Sensitization Assessment.
papers.abstract: Skin sensitization remains a critical toxicological endpoint in cosmetic ingredient development, particularly under accelerated innovation cycles and increasingly stringent safety requirements. Although NAMs have achieved substantial regulatory maturity for this endpoint, most computational approaches-including structural alerts, read-across, and quantitative structure-activity relationship models-rely predominantly on chemical structure and statistical associations, with limited representation of the molecular processes underlying sensitization. This perspective proposes a transparent and tes
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current computational toxicology methods for assessing skin sensitization—such as structural alerts and QSAR models—rely too heavily on chemical structure and statistical correlations, missing the underlying molecular mechanisms. The authors propose integrating molecular dynamics simulations and artificial intelligence to create more transparent, mechanistically grounded next-generation models for cosmetic safety assessment.

papers.title: Dioscin attenuates D‑galactose‑induced retinal pigment epithelium senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via the TGF‑β2/PI3K/Akt/β‑catenin pathway.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of Dioscin in an age-related macular degeneration (AMD) -like model and to explore its potential therapeutic mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether dioscin, a natural steroidal saponin, can protect retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells from senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in a D-galactose-induced model of age-related macular degeneration. The authors report that dioscin's protective effects are mediated through the TGF-β2/PI3K/Akt/β-catenin signaling pathway, suggesting a potential therapeutic avenue for AMD.

papers.title: A Hypoxia Associated STC2 High Endothelial Subpopulation is Linked to Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming, Pathological Angiogenesis, and Immune Remodeling in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia drives malignant advancement and immune escape in HNSCC, but its cell‑type‑specific regulatory circuitry within the TME remains insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically characterizes hypoxia‑associated molecular programs and identifies core genes with relevance to prognosis and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This study characterizes hypoxia-associated molecular programs in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying a STC2-high endothelial subpopulation linked to lipid metabolic reprogramming, pathological angiogenesis, and immune remodeling. The findings highlight cell-type-specific hypoxia responses within the tumor microenvironment and nominate core genes with prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates tolerogenic dendritic cell (tolDC) transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptome datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDCs to keloid pathology. The authors identify key tolDC-associated genes and perform preliminary mRNA validation, suggesting a potential immunoregulatory role for tolDCs in keloid formation. The findings provide a starting point for understanding immune mechanisms in keloid but require further experimental validation.

papers.title: An interpretable consensus pipeline for candidate dopamine D2 receptor ligands.
papers.abstract: Machine learning accelerates GPCR ligand discovery but often lacks interpretability and struggles to generalise to structurally novel chemical space. We present an integrated framework combining ensemble learning, SHAP interpretability, and complementary structure-based analyses to prioritise putative candidates for the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2). Models were trained on 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds using Bemis-Murcko scaffold-split validation. Feature ablation showed that Morgan fingerprints alone were sufficient for classification (AUC = 0.910), whereas combined physicochemical descriptors
papers.summary: The authors present an interpretable machine-learning pipeline that combines ensemble learning, SHAP explainability, and structure-based analyses to prioritize candidate ligands for the dopamine D2 receptor. Trained on 1247 curated ChEMBL compounds with scaffold-split validation, the models achieved strong classification performance (AUC = 0.910) using Morgan fingerprints alone, suggesting physicochemical descriptors add little value.

papers.title: MAFF as a potential novel protective factor against Parkinson's disease: evidence from Mendelian randomization and single-cell RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder. Although MAFF may be involved in PD, the mechanisms underlying this association remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the potential mechanisms of MAFF in PD and identify novel therapeutic targets.
papers.summary: This study combines Mendelian randomization with single-cell RNA sequencing to investigate whether the transcription factor MAFF protects against Parkinson's disease. The authors find evidence suggesting MAFF acts as a potential protective factor, implicating it as a possible novel therapeutic target for PD.

papers.title: Bioinspired and Biomimetic Nanocarriers: Advances in Exosomes and Cell-Membrane-Coated Systems for Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: The translation of nanomedicine from bench to bedside has been thwarted by the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles including rapid mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) clearance, lack of target specificity, immunogenicity and poor intracellular delivery. To overcome these limitations, bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers are emerging as the next generation of therapeutic platforms. Bioinspired systems replicate the core biological design principles with engineered synthetic materials and biomimetic platforms use natural biological components such as cell membranes and extracel
papers.summary: This review examines bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers, particularly exosomes and cell-membrane-coated systems, as next-generation therapeutic platforms that overcome the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles such as rapid immune clearance, poor targeting, and immunogenicity. It surveys how these systems replicate natural biological design principles to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Structure based discovery of VMP-7 as a promising GlgE targeting lead against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel drug targets with high specificity and therapeutic potential. Maltosyltransferase (GlgE) is a critical enzyme in the biosynthesis of cytosolic α-glucan, a key component required for maintaining cell wall integrity and intracellular survival of the pathogen. GlgE catalyzes the transfer of maltosyl units from maltose-1-phosphate to elongating α-glucan chains, and its inactivation results in toxic accumulation of metabolic intermediates, ultimately lea
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based drug discovery to identify VMP-7 as a lead compound targeting GlgE, a key enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall biosynthesis. GlgE inactivation leads to toxic metabolite accumulation and bacterial death, making it an attractive drug target. VMP-7 shows promise as a starting point for developing new anti-TB therapeutics.
